title: 2012 AMC 12A Problem 10
statement: A triangle has area \(30,\) one side of length \(10,\) and the median to that side of length \(9.\) Let \(\theta\) be the acute angle formed by that side and the median. What is \(\sin\theta?\)

solutions.text:
The median divides the triangle into two triangles of equal area \(15.\) One of them has the two sides of length \(5\) (half the base) and \(9\) (the median) meeting at angle \(\theta.\)

Its area is \(\tfrac12 \cdot 5 \cdot 9 \sin\theta = 15,\) so \(\sin\theta = \dfrac{2 \cdot 15}{5 \cdot 9} = \dfrac{2}{3}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: A median splits a triangle into two pieces of equal area
One half-triangle has sides \(5\) and \(9\) with included angle \(\theta\) and area \(15\)
